lesson_defects: The lesson never teaches the banishments of Roger Williams and Anne Hutchinson, which the keys of MCQ 0160 and 0163 hinge on — the lesson contains zero mentions of Williams, Hutchinson or banishment, and neither stimulus mentions them. Fix: one or two sentences in the 'Covenants and charters' section.

The lesson teaches the fact of salutary neglect but never the reason London left the colonies alone, which MCQ 0192's key requires (distance, European wars, Walpole's priorities). Fix: one sentence in 'The empire loosens its grip'.

The lesson dates Maryland's founding to 1633 (line 145) while LEQ 0013's model outline and rubric say 1634. One date must govern; 1634 is the conventional founding date (Ark and Dove arrived March 1634).
lesson_notes: Lesson is otherwise accurate and internally consistent: Jamestown 144/38 and starving-time figures, 350,000 Spaniards by 1650, 20,000+ to Massachusetts Bay 1630-1642, France few settlers/no exact count, Dominion 1686-1689, Georgia rules gone by 1751 and royal colony 1752 — all check against the questions and the books. The Georgia stimulus sentence is the one that misleads (see 0190), not the lesson.
